sentiment.rationale: The document reports strong Q4 and FY2026 results, with revenue and adjusted operating income growing 8% year-over-year. More importantly, management introduced a CY2026 outlook with adjusted EPS of $16.90 to $18.10, implying 20% growth in the June-through-December transition year, which is a clear forward guidance raise. The tone is confident, with management stating 'our profitable growth strategy is working' and 'we are building momentum.' However, the guidance includes headwinds from variable compensation and the new pilot contract, and the document acknowledges ongoing risks from global trade policy changes, preventing a higher score.

summary.revenue: Q4 FY2026 consolidated revenue was $25.0 billion, up 13% year-over-year. Full-year FY2026 revenue was $94.7 billion, up 8% year-over-year.
summary.eps: Q4 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $6.60; adjusted diluted EPS was $6.31. Full-year FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $18.55; adjusted diluted EPS was $20.24.
summary.guidance: For calendar year 2026, FedEx forecasts revenue growth of approximately 11% year-over-year and adjusted diluted EPS from continuing operations of $16.90 to $18.10. For the June-through-December transition year, adjusted EPS is expected to be approximately $11.30, representing 20% year-over-year growth.
summary.margin: Q4 FY2026 GAAP operating margin was 6.2%; adjusted operating margin was 8.4%. Full-year FY2026 GAAP operating margin was 5.8%; adjusted operating margin was 7.0%. At Federal Express segment, full-year adjusted operating margin was 7.7%, the highest in four years.
key_risks: Global trade policy changes and uncertainty in the global trade environment.
Higher purchased transportation and wage rates.
Grounding of MD-11 aircraft fleet (though returning to service).
Potential adverse economic, geopolitical, or international trade-related developments.
Stranded costs from the FedEx Freight spin-off (approximately $350 million remaining).
key_opportunities: Continued strength in U.S. Domestic and International Priority package yields.
Cost savings from transformation initiatives (Network 2.0, Tricolor, Europe restructuring).
Growth in high-value verticals: healthcare ($10 billion revenue), AI/data centers (double-digit growth).
International export package volume growth (up 5% in Q4).
FedEx Freight spin-off positions both companies for focused growth.
Strong free cash flow generation ($4.7 billion in FY2026) supporting capital returns.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management states 'our profitable growth strategy is working' and 'I have never been more confident on our path ahead,' reflecting strong conviction in the forward outlook.
